instruction: Navigate to discussions and open the thread that has been replied to the most times by users.

metadata.explanation: Task instructs user to find and open the most-replied discussion thread. Evaluator validates navigation to the correct target URL.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic gap: Instruction requires finding 'the thread that has been replied to the most times', but evaluator only checks if user navigated to a hardcoded URL
Evaluator does not verify that the target thread actually has the most replies - it assumes the answer is '/t/the-banter-thread/4412' without validation
This is a dynamic verification task (reply counts change over time), but the evaluator uses a static expected URL
The getter 'active_tab_info' only retrieves URL/title/content - it does not extract or compare reply counts across threads
The metric 'is_expected_active_tab' only performs URL comparison - it cannot validate the 'most replied' requirement
Evaluator would incorrectly pass if user directly navigated to the hardcoded URL without actually checking reply counts
Evaluator would incorrectly fail if user correctly identified a different thread that genuinely has more replies
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use 'get_info_from_website' getter to scrape the discussions page and extract reply counts for all threads
Create a new metric function that compares reply counts and identifies the thread with the maximum replies
Expected value should be computed dynamically from actual discussion data, not hardcoded
Alternative: Change instruction to 'Navigate to discussions and open the thread at /t/the-banter-thread/4412' to match the static evaluator
Or use HTML parsing to extract reply counts from thread list elements and verify the opened thread has the highest count
